findings.sectionRef: Approach > Files to Create/Modify; Acceptance Criteria > AC-2
findings.description: Manual publish-sandbox-patch.md Step 5 (L304) copies only codex.exe + codex-core.exe, while CI publish-npm.yml (L139-142) packs all four exes + rg.exe. Since Step 5 is the primary release path (CI org-blocked), the R2 bundle the installer extracts would be incomplete. Flagged by Claude, Codex, and Copilot; confirmed by direct read of L304.
findings.resolution: Made the Step 5 binary-set reconciliation an in-scope hard requirement (US-002) and added AC-2b asserting the published tarball contains the full 5-artifact set. Moved out of Open Questions into in-scope.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the two missing cp lines to Step 5; assert the tarball binary set in the publish helper.

findings.description: The helper uploaded release objects (tarball/sha256/manifest/latest) but nothing published install.ps1 / install.sh to the R2 root. The one-liner `irm https://codex.evyatar.dev/install.ps1 | iex` depends on those static objects existing and matching the repo source. Flagged by Codex and Copilot.
findings.resolution: Helper (US-001) now uploads/syncs install.ps1 and install.sh to the R2 root keys /install.ps1 and /install.sh; added AC-2c verifying byte-match to the repo sources.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a helper mode/AC to upload and keep the installer scripts in sync.

findings.description: AC-2 required shared manifest logic but not that the uploaded tarball contains the full Windows binary set; a correct manifest could be published over wrong tarball contents. Flagged by Claude and Codex.
findings.resolution: Added AC-2b asserting codex.exe, codex-core.exe, codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe, codex-command-runner.exe, and rg.exe are present; a manifest over an incomplete tarball fails the check.
findings.suggestedFix: Assert the full binary set in the publish path.

findings.description: The flat ~/.codex-fork/ layout makes install-context/src/lib.rs classify the install as Other, and tui/src/update_action.rs:25 returns UpdateAction::None for Other — disabling native codex self-update. The plan only noted doctor 'follow-up' in prose.
findings.resolution: Elevated to an explicit Architecture decision with the self-update consequence stated. Default: ~/.codex-fork/bin/ + codex-package.json marker; US-003 verifies install-context classification (AC-11); if unsatisfiable, native self-update is a documented v1 limitation (upgrade = re-run one-liner) + follow-up. Open Question 1 reframed; decision required before US-003.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt a recognized layout or explicitly accept/follow-up the self-update limitation.

findings.sectionRef: Approach > install.ps1 algorithm step 5; Acceptance Criteria > AC-5
findings.description: 'Terminate running codex/codex-core processes' was too broad — it could kill an unrelated npm-global install or an active session elsewhere on the machine.
findings.resolution: Algorithm step 5 now scopes the kill to processes whose exe path is under the install root, prompts unless CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE; AC-5 verifies an unrelated codex process outside the install root is left running.
findings.suggestedFix: Scope process termination to the target install root.

findings.description: 'Atomically swap into the install dir' is underspecified for Windows directories — replacing a non-empty directory is not atomic; partial rename/delete failure could leave no working install.
findings.resolution: Algorithm step 6 now specifies stage -> backup current -> rename staging into place -> rollback-on-failure from backup; AC-5 verifies rollback leaves the prior install intact.

findings.description: AC-3 said 'launcher starts', but first-run can prompt/login — ambiguous for an autonomous test. Flagged by Codex and Copilot.
findings.resolution: AC-3 now uses CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 and exact verification: fresh powershell -NoProfile finds codex on PATH, codex --version succeeds, rg.exe resolvable from the same PATH entry, extracted bin/ layout matches.

findings.description: Installer authoring was allowed in parallel after the manifest contract is 'fixed', but the install layout and manifest URL shape were still open — risking incompatible installer/docs assumptions.
findings.resolution: Added a 'Prerequisite decisions (resolve BEFORE US-003 begins)' note covering install layout and manifest URL shape; Open Questions 1 and 4 flagged as 'decision needed before US-003 starts'.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve layout + URL shape before US-003.

findings.sectionRef: Approach > Architecture (R2 interface); Acceptance Criteria > AC-2; Open Questions
findings.description: R2 upload mechanism was underspecified ('wrangler or S3 PUT') without choosing one or naming exact env vars/secrets, no-op behavior, or dry-run mode.
findings.resolution: Chose a default (S3-compatible PUT) with named env vars (R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/R2_ACCOUNT_ID|R2_S3_ENDPOINT/R2_BUCKET), wrangler as documented alternative, no-op-without-creds + --dry-run/--local-out mode; documented in Architecture, AC-2, and Open Question 5.
findings.suggestedFix: Pick one interface; name env vars; specify no-op + dry-run.

findings.description: A flat layout makes the installer do extra work (rg.exe co-location, follow-up doctor/update support) that the recognized package layout would avoid.
findings.resolution: Folded into the F-004 layout decision: default now uses ~/.codex-fork/bin + codex-package.json marker to attempt the recognized package_layout, with the standalone layout offered as the operator's up-front Option 2; trade-off documented.

findings.sectionRef: Approach > install.ps1 algorithm step 7; Acceptance Criteria > AC-3
findings.description: Re-review round 2: PATH wiring used only SetEnvironmentVariable('User') (registry), but AC-3 expected a same-session/child process to find codex immediately. A child inherits the parent process env, not the just-written registry value, so the one-liner (irm|iex) case would not work until a new shell opened.
findings.resolution: Algorithm step 7 now updates BOTH the persistent user PATH (registry, for new shells) AND $env:Path in the current session; AC-3 verifies both same-session (codex --version succeeds immediately) and persistent (registry entry present once).
findings.suggestedFix: Update $env:Path in-session in addition to the registry write.

findings.sectionRef: Approach > Architecture (R2 interface); Acceptance Criteria > AC-2
findings.description: Re-review round 2: the helper no-op'd non-fatally on missing R2 creds, but the manual publish-sandbox-patch.md Step 5 is the authoritative release path. A release could succeed (GitHub asset published) while silently skipping the R2 upload, leaving the public one-liner broken for that version.
findings.resolution: Made credential-absence path-dependent: CI step keeps the non-fatal no-op; the manual Step 5 invocation fails by default unless --skip-r2/--dry-run is explicitly passed. Documented in Architecture and AC-2.
findings.suggestedFix: Manual path: hard-fail on missing creds unless explicitly skipped.

findings.description: Re-review round 2: an S3-compatible 'PUT' to R2 omitted the SigV4 signing/dependency detail — a plain HTTP PUT fails. No existing R2 helper to reuse.
findings.resolution: Flipped the default to `wrangler r2 object put` (native R2 auth, no hand-rolled signing); documented that the S3-compatible alternative requires a SigV4 signer dependency (aws4fetch or @aws-sdk/client-s3) and that the dependency choice is part of US-001.
findings.suggestedFix: Use wrangler, or specify a SigV4 signer dependency for the S3 path.

findings.description: Re-review round 2: AC-3 did not state exactly how PATH visibility is verified (same-session vs new-terminal), leaving the 'fresh powershell' check unreliable.
findings.resolution: AC-3 now specifies two-way verification: same-session (codex --version immediately after the script returns) and persistent (user PATH registry contains the bin dir exactly once).

findings.description: Re-review round 3: US-001 still said 'default S3-compatible PUT' while Architecture + Open Question 5 said the default is wrangler — a self-contradiction that could send implementers down the SigV4 path.
findings.resolution: US-001 corrected to 'default pinned npx -y wrangler@<pinned> r2 object put' (the round-2 Architecture flip is now consistent across Approach, Open Question 5, US-001, AC-2).
findings.suggestedFix: Make US-001 match the wrangler default.

findings.sectionRef: Approach > Architecture (R2 interface); Acceptance Criteria > AC-2
findings.description: Re-review round 3: with wrangler as the default, neither publish-npm.yml nor the manual Step 5 sets wrangler up; the plan didn't specify how wrangler is made available in either path.
findings.resolution: Added a 'wrangler availability' contract: the helper uses a pinned `npx -y wrangler@<pinned>` (no global install assumed; Node present in both paths) and prerequisite-checks wrangler/network, hard-failing the manual path with a clear message; AC-2 asserts this and the CI/manual docs reflect it.
findings.suggestedFix: Pin npx wrangler or add explicit setup + a prerequisite check.

findings.sectionRef: Approach > Architecture (publish ordering); Acceptance Criteria > AC-1
findings.description: Re-review round 3: the helper lacked a partial-publish ordering contract — a failed publish could leave /latest pointing at a version whose manifest or tarball is missing, breaking install.ps1.
findings.resolution: Added a mandatory ordering contract: upload {tarball, .sha256, manifest.json, install.ps1, install.sh} first, verify each, then write /latest LAST; abort without touching /latest on any pre-/latest failure. AC-1 now asserts /latest-last + that a simulated mid-publish failure leaves /latest unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Write /latest last, after all other objects are verified.

findings.description: Re-review round 3: AC-2 did not assert wrangler availability/setup despite wrangler being the default upload interface.
findings.resolution: AC-2 now requires the pinned npx wrangler usage + manual-path prerequisite hard-fail (same remediation as F-016, AC angle).
findings.suggestedFix: Add a wrangler-availability verification point to AC-2.
